name: What is the difference between a room addition and a bump-out?

mainEntity.name: How do I know whether I need a true addition or just a small extension?
mainEntity.text: How do I know whether I need a true addition or just a small extension?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out is best understood as a smaller-scale extension of an existing room. It might widen a kitchen, enlarge a bathroom, or add a few feet to a bedroom. A full room addition, by contrast, creates new usable space that functions as a separate part of the home. The distinction matters because the design, structural work, and budget are very different. Bump-outs are usually less disruptive and can sometimes avoid the complexity of major foundation or roof work, but they also provide limited benefit. If the real problem is a missing bedroom, a cramped primary suite, or a lack of family space, a bump-out may not be enough. Homeowners should think about the goal first: if the issue is circulation or storage, a small extension may work; if the issue is overall livability, a larger addition is usually the better investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out is a small extension of an existing room, often just a few feet, while a full room addition creates a new functional space such as a bedroom, bathroom, or family room. Bump-outs are usually simpler and cheaper, but they add less value and may not solve larger space problems.
